## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG and no intermediate storage can approach the streaming ceiling by keeping the death verdict in registers.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout offers loop 1 only 32 hot bytes (47% — age+pos+seed+vel) and loop 2 only 28 (41% — color+pos); the rest is dead line-filler. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers. The approach fuses integrate+decide+respawn into one scalar pass with cmovae-based death handling and byte-granular color scatter. With under half the bytes hot, useful bandwidth is halved before compute, and the 68 B stride means each particle spans just over one cache line.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p is strikingly flat: at q=0.01, 34.6 ns/p at N=320 (L1d) vs 34.8 at N=10M (DRAM) — no cache-spill knee. A minor rise to ~37.5 in L2/L3 (N=3100–19000) settles back in DRAM. The L1d→L2 transition at N≈481 and L2→L3 at N≈7710 are invisible. Cost is compute- and branch-dominated, not data-movement-bound — cache residency is irrelevant when the loop is instruction-bound.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 1.65–1.97 GB/s against a 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 13–15% of peak. The 5.359 ns/p floor means memory is at most 15% of the 34–41 ns/p runtime: compute-and-branch-bound. Against baseline: 1.56x at q=0.01 N=320, declining to 1.19x at q=0.5 N=10M. Against the winner: 4.66x slower at q=0.01 N=320, narrowing to 2.19x at q=0.5 N=10M — death rate is the equalizer, but the gap never closes.

## Assembly
The codegen is scalar: 19 vector insns out of 413, almost all vmovaps for stack setup. The hot loop uses vmulss, vaddss, vsubss (scalar SP FP) and vucomiss for death checks — no packed FP. The digest confirms ~192 insns/iter, 21 conditional branches, 12 cmovae selects, and 16 byte-granular stores (movzx+add+cmp+cmovae+strb). The death path is vucomiss→jae/jne chains, not a pure blend. This explains the 15% ceiling utilization: the loop cannot issue enough outstanding loads to saturate memory, and 21 branches/iter cost ~20% in branch_flush.

## Verdict
Refuted — at 34.6 ns/p (q=0.01, N=320) the algo is 6.5x above the 5.359 ns/p floor and 4.66x slower than the autovec winner, achieving 1.97 of 12.69 GB/s. The codegen is scalar FP with 21 branches/iter and byte-granular scatter — not the branchless blend assumed — and branch_flush holds at 20% across all regimes. The flat ns/p from L1d through DRAM confirms compute/branch dominance. Only at q=0.5 does the winner gap narrow to 2.19x, and even there it never exceeds 1.23x over baseline.
